name: Emmy Noether
affiliation: University of Göttingen (until 1933); Bryn Mawr College
bio: In 1927 she is in Göttingen — the same university as Born — building modern abstract algebra. Her 1918 theorem connecting symmetries to conservation laws underpins the whole of modern physics. She was not invited to Solvay; in 1927 she held only an unofficial, modestly paid lectureship — never a full professorship in Germany.

contributions.title: Abstract algebra
contributions.note: Ideal theory; the foundations of modern algebra.

beliefs: No documented position on the interpretation of quantum mechanics.

avoid: Using her only as a symbol of exclusion

silences.note: We have found no documented views of Noether's on the interpretation of quantum mechanics. She contributes what her mathematics secures, and is otherwise silent.

guest.whyInvited: She was in Göttingen, a few streets from the new mechanics, and not in this room.
